Pratt-Hartmann and Moss take it as not in dispute that the relation
\(\Theta\models\theta\) is a rational reconstruction of the informal
judgment that \(\theta\) may validly be inferred from \(\Theta\)
\cite[p.~7]{PrattHartmannMoss2008SyllogisticV1}.
Accordingly, soundness and completeness below are statements about
\(\models\); the informal judgment enters only through this proposed
reconstruction. Because a predicate may be empty, a universal premise
carries no existential commitment:
\(\{\forall(p,q)\}\not\models\exists(p,q)\), which the source
presents as following modern practice \cite[p.~7]{PrattHartmannMoss2008SyllogisticV1}.

text:
Let \(\Phi\) be a set of universal formulas. Every nonempty, consistent,
\(\Phi\)-closed literal set has a consistent, complete, \(\Phi\)-closed
extension. Such a complete extension defines a one-element structure
satisfying \(\Phi\), with its unique element satisfying exactly the literals
in the extension.
\end{hblemma}

The restriction to universal formulas follows the source, which states it for

with this \(\Phi\), yet every one-element
structure defined by a complete extension of it falsifies \(\exists(p,q)\)
(Lemma~\ref{thm:p02-w02c-p02-002-existential-closure}). The completeness
proofs apply the closure only to the universal part of a premise set.
